title: Germany by Rail in 23 Days: Munich, Leipzig, Dresden, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Heidelberg and Stuttgart
meta_title: Germany Grand Rail Tour 23 Days: Munich to Stuttgart
meta_description: 23-day Germany rail tour: Munich and Neuschwanstein, Leipzig, Dresden, Berlin and Potsdam, Hamburg, Cologne, the Rhine, Heidelberg and the Black Forest.
tagline: Ten German cities by fast train, two nights or more in each
facts: Munich 3, Leipzig 2, Dresden 2, Berlin 2, Hamburg 2, Hannover 2, Cologne 2, Frankfurt 2, Heidelberg 2, Stuttgart 3
ICE and regional trains, 1 to 3 hours each
Relaxed; two nights or more everywhere
May to September, or December for Christmas markets
intro: A slow, complete journey through Germany by train, with at least two nights in every city. Bavaria's castles from Munich, the music city of Leipzig, baroque Dresden, Berlin and the palaces of Potsdam, the port of Hamburg, Hannover's gardens, Cologne Cathedral, Frankfurt and the Rhine Valley, the castle of Heidelberg with a day in Baden-Baden and the Black Forest, and the car museums of Stuttgart. We updated the original plan: the Pergamon Museum in Berlin is closed for renovation until about 2027, so you visit the Neues Museum instead; we moved the Black Forest day to Heidelberg, which is closer; and Frankfurt now has a Rhine Valley day.
highlights: Neuschwanstein and Linderhof, King Ludwig's castles
Bach's Leipzig and the rebuilt Frauenkirche in Dresden
The Brandenburg Gate, the Berlin Wall and Museum Island
Hamburg's harbour, Speicherstadt and the Elbphilharmonie
Cologne Cathedral and a Rhine cruise
The Rhine Valley's castles and the Loreley rock
Heidelberg Castle and the Old Bridge
Baden-Baden's thermal baths and the Black Forest

good_to_know.title: German trains
good_to_know.text: Fast ICE trains link every city on this route. A German Rail Pass or advance tickets with seat reservations work best; we compare the two for your dates.

good_to_know.title: Sundays
good_to_know.text: Almost all shops are closed on Sundays in Germany. Plan shopping for Saturday.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in euros, never in INR. Cards work almost everywhere. Carry about EUR 50 in cash for small cafés, toilets and markets.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

best_time: May to September for river cruises, gardens and beer gardens. Late November and December for Germany's Christmas markets.
seasons: Warm days (20 to 26°C), beer gardens and river cruises; long evenings.

best_pick: May, June or September; December for Christmas markets.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

dining_intro: Vegetarian food is easy to find in every city on this route; Jain meals take planning. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and tour, and list Indian and vegetarian restaurants near each hotel in your travel pack.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
